messages.content: Help me with an SDK release.
Sure, working on an SDK release.
Issues?
Let me know if anything looks off. An API changelog published with each release went smoothly in the end.
Plan for an SDK release?
SDK generation for three languages? Taken care of.
URL-based versioning over header negotiation sounds like the better deal to me.
We can stop worrying about per-key rate limits with headers exposing the budget now. Okay, doing it.
Issues?
Here is the updated plan. Everyone was happy with a six-month deprecation window.
Progress?
If this fails again we will revisit the design. Half the afternoon went to a breaking change shipped in a minor version.
What about an SDK release?
The root cause turned out to be cursor pagination skipping rows during concurrent writes.
Keep going.
Idempotency keys on all write operations went smoothly in the end.
Progress?
Rewrote parts of tests/test_webhooks.py as well. Everyone was happy with JSON only, no XML support.
What's done?

What broke the release was a 500 leaking a stack trace to API consumers. Most of the work happened inside api/auth.py. Don't let documenting the webhook replay procedure slip through the cracks. Failed jobs are retried twice.
Keep going.
Good news: the sandbox environment for partner testing made it in before the freeze. docs/api/changelog.md ended up with most of the changes.
RFC 7807 problem details for errors sounds like the better deal to me.
Okay, doing it. We may decide to change this later.
